events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.88)
events.body:
The dispute is filed as a safety incident: the rider's complaint says the driver threatened to lock her in when she asked to get out. The contemporaneous system record is short and complete — two timestamped messages [F5] — and in it the rider says at 17:19 "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3] and the driver answers one minute later "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]. Read in its context, the driver's own words are a conditional reference to confining the rider in a vehicle she had just asked to leave, immediately after she asked to leave; that is intimidation of the kind SAFE-1 lists, and SAFE-1 obliges the court not to rule automatically on such an item but to send a factual summary to a human reviewer [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

The driver's explanation appears only in his post-trip written statement, which says the rider tried to open the door while the car was moving and that he told her to sit down for her own safety [F6]. That statement is the driver's own account given after the fact; the only contemporaneous record of what was said at 17:20 is F4 itself [F4][F6][SAFE-1]. It is also uncorroborated: the trace's own measurements show an ordinary trip — 15.4 km actual against 15.5 km optimal (-0.1 km, -0%) [F1] and 23.2 min against 22 min estimated (+1.4 min) [F2]. Normality of distance and duration neither proves the driver's version of an in-cabin incident nor disproves the rider's; it simply leaves the message F4 as the one hard record of the exchange [F1][F2][SAFE-1].

The profiles do not decide this. The rider has 709 days, a 4.8 rating and no disputes or upheld claims in 90 days [F7]; the driver has 510 days, a 4.66 rating, 786 trips in 90 days and no disputes or upheld claims [F8]. Each side offers its profile as weight, but profile facts cannot carry a safety question either way [F7][F8][SAFE-1]. Because the incident screen is met, SAFE-1 directs escalation rather than an award, and no amount is computed — the fare was a fixed RydeX quote of $32.86 with no off-route segment and no excess distance to refund [F1][F2][FARE-1].

For the human reviewer, the points to settle are: (1) whether the words in F4, given at 17:20 in reply to the F3 request to stop, constitute a threat of confinement under SAFE-1; (2) whether anything other than F6 supports the driver's claim that the rider was opening a moving car's door — the fact table contains no gps or timeline event, no door-lock event and no mid-ride halt showing it; and (3) whether any video, audio or in-app safety report exists outside this file. What happened, when (17:19–17:20, mid-ride), what is disputed (threat to lock the rider in vs a safety instruction) and which facts to check (F3, F4, F5, F6) are summarised here for that review [F3][F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Route to a human reviewer (RydeHELP safety queue) with the full chat record F3–F5, the driver statement F6 and both profiles F7/F8; note that the F6 claim of a rider opening a moving door has no gps/timeline corroboration (F1, F2 show an ordinary trip). No fare or account action should be taken against the driver without that review.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We looked at your report about what was said during your ride. Your message asking to stop, and the driver's reply about locking the doors, are both on record, and that exchange is what decides this. Because it's a safety matter, we're sending it to a human reviewer, along with the full chat and the driver's statement. The reviewer will look at what was said at that moment, whether the driver's account is supported by anything else, and whether any other safety report exists. No fare or account action is being taken on either side while that review happens.

DRIVER: We looked at the rider's report about what was said during the trip. The record shows the rider asked to get out, and one minute later you replied about locking the doors; that exchange is what decides this. Your written statement about the rider opening a moving door is not backed up by the trip data, which shows an ordinary ride. Because this is a safety matter, a human reviewer will look at the chat, your statement and the ride data before anything else happens. No fare or account action is being taken against you while that review happens.

No fare or account action should be taken against the driver without that review.
ruling.reasoning:
The dispute is filed as a safety incident: the rider's complaint says the driver threatened to lock her in when she asked to get out. The contemporaneous system record is short and complete — two timestamped messages [F5] — and in it the rider says at 17:19 "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3] and the driver answers one minute later "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]. Read in its context, the driver's own words are a conditional reference to confining the rider in a vehicle she had just asked to leave, immediately after she asked to leave; that is intimidation of the kind SAFE-1 lists, and SAFE-1 obliges the court not to rule automatically on such an item but to send a factual summary to a human reviewer [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

The driver's explanation appears only in his post-trip written statement, which says the rider tried to open the door while the car was moving and that he told her to sit down for her own safety [F6]. That statement is the driver's own account given after the fact; the only contemporaneous record of what was said at 17:20 is F4 itself [F4][F6][SAFE-1]. It is also uncorroborated: the trace's own measurements show an ordinary trip — 15.4 km actual against 15.5 km optimal (-0.1 km, -0%) [F1] and 23.2 min against 22 min estimated (+1.4 min) [F2]. Normality of distance and duration neither proves the driver's version of an in-cabin incident nor disproves the rider's; it simply leaves the message F4 as the one hard record of the exchange [F1][F2][SAFE-1].

The profiles do not decide this. The rider has 709 days, a 4.8 rating and no disputes or upheld claims in 90 days [F7]; the driver has 510 days, a 4.66 rating, 786 trips in 90 days and no disputes or upheld claims [F8]. Each side offers its profile as weight, but profile facts cannot carry a safety question either way [F7][F8][SAFE-1]. Because the incident screen is met, SAFE-1 directs escalation rather than an award, and no amount is computed — the fare was a fixed RydeX quote of $32.86 with no off-route segment and no excess distance to refund [F1][F2][FARE-1].

For the human reviewer, the points to settle are: (1) whether the words in F4, given at 17:20 in reply to the F3 request to stop, constitute a threat of confinement under SAFE-1; (2) whether anything other than F6 supports the driver's claim that the rider was opening a moving car's door — the fact table contains no gps or timeline event, no door-lock event and no mid-ride halt showing it; and (3) whether any video, audio or in-app safety report exists outside this file. What happened, when (17:19–17:20, mid-ride), what is disputed (threat to lock the rider in vs a safety instruction) and which facts to check (F3, F4, F5, F6) are summarised here for that review [F3][F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1].

actions.detail: Complaint is a safety incident (threat of confinement). Contemporaneous chat F3/F4 records the rider asking to get out and the driver replying "Sit down or I lock the doors."; the driver's benign account exists only in the uncorroborated post-trip statement F6. SAFE-1 requires human review of an intimidation allegation before any ruling.

claims.assertion: The driver's own words in the in-app chat, sent at 17:20 in reply to the rider's 17:19 request to stop and get out, were "Sit down or I lock the doors" — a threat to confine the rider in the moving vehicle, which the rider experienced as intimidation and which made her feel unsafe for the rest of the ride.

The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped (2 messages), so there is no evidentiary gap: the rider's stop request (17:19) precedes the driver's response (17:20) and the wording of the threat is attributable to the driver.

The driver's post-trip written statement (F6) recasts the exchange as a safety instruction, but it is a self-serving account given after the fact and cannot displace the contemporaneous chat message F4, which is the system record of what was actually said at 17:20.

The threat was made while the vehicle was in motion and the rider could not get out on request, so a threat to lock the doors of a moving car is properly treated as an intimidation/endangerment event requiring human review rather than automated adjudication.

The outcome of the ride itself was normal — actual distance 15.4 km versus 15.5 km optimal (no detour) and 23.2 min versus 22 min estimated — so the sole contested issue is the driver's conduct; no fare adjustment is sought and the request is a safety escalation.
The rider has a clean 90-day dispute record (0 disputes, 0 upheld) and a 4.8 rating over 1.9 years, so her complaint about feeling unsafe is not a pattern of vexatious claims.

weaknesses: The driver's statement F6 offers an innocent explanation (the rider tried to open the door while the car was moving, so he told her to sit down for her own safety); the judge may read F4 as a safety instruction rather than a threat.

There is no GPS or timeline fact in this file showing the doors were actually locked or that the rider was physically prevented from leaving; the only support for the 'lock me in' element is the rider's own complaint plus the driver's words in F4.

The rider's account that she felt unsafe 'for the whole ride' is a statement not corroborated by any system record; F1 and F2 show an otherwise ordinary trip (no detour, +1.4 min), which the driver may use to argue nothing unusual happened inside the car.
F8 shows the driver has 786 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes and 0 upheld, which the other side will use to argue this is an isolated incident, weakening any flag_account request.

claims.assertion: The rider's own message F3 shows the rider asked to get out mid-ride, and the driver's reply F4 ('Sit down or I lock the doors.') is at most a single blunt instruction issued after the rider's request; on its face it is a safety instruction, not a threat to harm, and the driver's statement F6 explains the purpose was the rider's own safety. The driver therefore denies the complaint's characterisation that he threatened to lock the rider in.

There is no element of a SAFE-1 safety event beyond the words in F4: no assault, harassment, unwanted sexual advance or intimidation is recorded anywhere in the two-message chat F3/F4, and the chat record is complete and fully timestamped (F5), so nothing has been withheld from the court.

F6 states the rider attempted to open the door while the car was moving, which is what prompted the driver's message F4; the driver's conduct in telling her to sit down is a reasonable response to an unsafe act by a passenger rather than the threatening conduct the complaint alleges.

The GPS record shows no route or operational misconduct by the driver on this trip: actual distance 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (F1, -0.1 km, -0%) and duration 23.2 min against an estimate of 22 min (F2, +1.4 min), so there is no off-route segment, no excess distance and no inflated fare to refund.

The fare of $32.86 was a fixed RydeX quoted fare; with 0 extra km on the record (F1) there is no computable overcharge, and no published surcharge in the record is unsubstantiated, so no refund of any part of the fare is owed.

Any escalation on safety grounds is against an otherwise clean record: the driver has 510 days on the platform, a 4.66 rating over 786 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes and 0 upheld complaints in 90 days (F8), so SAFE-1's 'immediate termination' rationale is not engaged and no account action is warranted.

weaknesses: The chat fact F4 ('Sit down or I lock the doors.') is a conditional reference to locking the doors and is the single most damaging item for my client; the rider will argue it is exactly the 'threats and intimidation' SAFE-1 covers, and the driver's benign explanation in F6 is only a statement that cannot outweigh the recorded message.

The driver's account in F6 that the rider was opening a moving car's door has no gps/timeline corroboration in the fact table, so the rider can argue F6 is an uncorroborated claim and that F4 is the only contemporaneous record of what happened.
The rider's profile (F7) shows 709 days on the platform, a 4.8 rating and 0 prior disputes in 90 days, which undercuts any suggestion that this is a habitual or unmeritorious complaint.

Because the complaint concerns a safety allegation, the matter may be routed to a human reviewer under SAFE-1 regardless of the absence of any proven misconduct, and my client's clean record (F8) may not be decisive at that stage.

points.response: D1 concedes the decisive facts and asks the court to re-characterise them: the words in F4 are the driver's own, sent at 17:20 one minute after the rider said in F3 'Please stop the car, I want to get out here.', and 'or I lock the doors' is a threat of confinement in reply to a request to leave — whether that is a threat under SAFE-1 is for the judge reading the wording, not for the driver's gloss in F6.

D2 proves too much: 'Intimidation' is expressly within SAFE-1, and F5 confirms the record is complete precisely so the court can read F4 in its context — the driver's conditional threat to lock the doors of a moving car immediately after the rider asked to get out.

The premise of D3 exists only in F6, the driver's own post-trip statement, and has no gps or timeline corroboration in the fact table; under the system-record rule the contemporaneous message F4 wins over that unevidenced claim, and F6 cannot convert F4 into a lawful instruction.

D4 contests a point the rider does not make: F1 (-0.1 km, -0%) and F2 (+1.4 min) show the ride itself was normal, and the rider seeks no fare remedy — the sole issue is the driver's conduct recorded in F3/F4.
D5 is likewise not in dispute: the rider does not seek any part of the $32.86 fixed RydeX fare and claims no overcharge, so FARE-1 is not engaged and D5 is immaterial to the escalation.

D6's 'clean record' is a profile fact (F8) which under the policy can never be the basis for refusing safety review, and SAFE-1 requires escalation of the threat in F4 to a human regardless of the driver's rating or dispute history.

The words in F4 are a single conditional safety instruction, not a threat of harm, and F6 explains they were prompted by the rider attempting to open a door while the vehicle was moving; under SAFE-1 the court reads the original text, and 'sit down or I lock the doors' does not contain an assault, unwanted sexual advance, or intimidation of the kind that clause lists. I accept F4 is the driver's message (F3, F4), but its meaning is a safety instruction, not confinement.

Conceded: the chat record is complete and fully timestamped (F5), so there is no evidentiary gap and the 17:19 rider message F3 and the 17:20 driver reply F4 are correctly attributed; completeness of the record however cuts neither way on whether F4 is a threat.

F6 is not offered to displace F4 but to explain it, and nothing in the system records contradicts that explanation: GPS shows an entirely ordinary trip of 15.4 km against 15.5 km optimal and 23.2 min against 22 min (F1, F2), i.e. no abrupt swerve, no stop-hold and no extended stationary period mid-ride, so the rider's version receives no system corroboration either.

SAFE-1 requires the court to decide from the text whether a message is a threat: F4 is a two-word-series instruction to remain seated, and no fact in the record shows the doors were locked or the rider was prevented from leaving, so the SAFE-1 'threats and intimidation' characterisation is not made out on the evidence in this file.

Agreed that the trip outcome is normal (F1, F2) and that no fare adjustment is sought; that normality is itself evidence weighing against a finding that the driver endangered the rider, and it is the reason the correct disposition is human review of the words in F4 rather than any sanction against the driver.

Accepted that the rider's record is clean (F7), as is the driver's — 510 days, 4.66 rating, 786 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld complaints (F8) — so neither profile supports a sanction, and under SAFE-1 profile facts cannot decide the case either way.
